searchText: I mean are they doing so though? Ethermine seems like the pool with the most invested in eth2 Hello guys. I have a wonder that how's transaction full lifecycle Post-Merge. In my understanding like below. ``` (user): sign_transaction >> (user) send_rawTransaction >> (EL client)receive transaction from user >> (EL client)Received_transaction_in_the_mempool >>(CL client) send engine_preparePayload to EL client >> (EL client) send engine_getpayload with Execution_payload which has user transaction to CL client >> (CL Client) get Execution_payload and send to EL client wich engine_execution_payload >> (EL client) respond to engine_execution_payload with blockHash and status to CL client >> (CL client) started to consensus process ``` Is this correct process ?? I have seen the https://hackmd.io/@n0ble/consensus_api_design_space#Block-proposal-flow This one <@!425572898787426305> written. But I'm not sure that process is same as actual implementation. You better look here, https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/specification.md -- this is the spec we ended up with. The transaction flow you have outlined looks correct in general, except fo `preparePayload` has been unified with `forkchoiceUpdated` which you can find in the spec Thank you so much Mikhail. I already have seen that specification, But those spec can't be understand easily. That's why I look your kind of `annotated`specification. you're welcome! GM! anyone seen any good illustrations of eth blocks? for documentation purposes Regarding with PBS proposal <@!273808422753796097> written, It's quite hard to understand why this research came out. Because of CALLDATA gas cost and related with EIP 4488?? That the hybrid PBS proposal possibly adopted in practice when verkle tree deployed. Isn't it? https://notes.ethereum.org/@vbuterin/pbs_censorship_resistance#Solution-2-can-we-still-use-proposers-%E2%80%9Chybrid-PBS%E2%80%9D-but-only-for-inclusion-of-last-resort If someone provided some context would be so much appreciated. I don't think that this PBS research doesn't comes out because of MEV only. You do raise a good point on cartel formation and IRL market practices (cornering the market / outright collusion / using non-public info, basically what whales do often in less well trafficked ethereum DeFi protocols) that are clearly banned in most credible meat space economies that are either rampant in crypto or are nascent but likely to be rampant and cause negative externalities for all other users. The question of what is or isn’t “legitimate” network activity begins to get murky i think once you go beyond blatant manipulation of gas market mechanisms I suppose this comes down to a couple issues: 1) protocol and incentive design (this point of this discord), 2) crypto education (the point of many other orgs within and beyond ethereum), and 3) fuzzy but very important alignment of cultural/social values that dictate onchain behavior (yes we need to design cryptoeconomic/cryptographic secure networks but values are impt too imo). But sorry this is veering off into a tangent. Back into my hole now That’s essentially a market structure problem no? Ie the relative market concentration of miners vs the bargaining power of searchers? I guess tbd how that evolves in a post-merge state of the world and how the validator set concentrates or (ideally) fragments over time Hasu did a good MEV deep dive on his pod with MEVintern. Way over my head so need to learn a bit more Yep. And as soon as more money is involved and someone wises up it’ll happen. Some Eth mining pools figured out they could use MEV 2+ years ago and did it for themselves to benefit their own trades. I completely expect some exchanges to prioritize themselves. Yes probably happens today too tbh. But post-merge, I suspect it'll show up when you see exchanges or other custodial-staking pools offering yields *well above* what should "naturally" occur, assuming they don't fund that incremental staking yield that their customers can earn themselves (wouldn't put it past the CEXs to "bribe" retail consumers given it may be beneficial for them to do so from a customer retention and new customer win rate standpoint) Binance could offer 1-2% over market and use their power to block other cexs Your totally right.

excerpts.author: johnydony
excerpts.content:
Hello guys. 
I have a wonder that how's transaction full lifecycle Post-Merge. 
In my understanding like below. 
```
(user): sign_transaction >> (user) send_rawTransaction >> (EL client)receive transaction from user >> (EL client)Received_transaction_in_the_mempool >>(CL client) send engine_preparePayload to EL client >> (EL client) send engine_getpayload with Execution_payload which has user transaction to CL client >> (CL Client) get Execution_payload and send to EL client wich engine_execution_payload >> (EL client) respond to engine_execution_payload with blockHash and status to CL client >> (CL client) started to consensus process 
```

excerpts.author: johnydony
excerpts.content: Is this correct process ??

excerpts.author: johnydony
excerpts.content:
I have seen the https://hackmd.io/@n0ble/consensus_api_design_space#Block-proposal-flow 
This one <@!425572898787426305>  written. 
But I'm not sure that process is same as actual implementation.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
You better look here, https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/specification.md -- this is the spec we ended up with.

The transaction flow you have outlined looks correct in general, except fo `preparePayload` has been unified with `forkchoiceUpdated` which you can find in the spec

excerpts.content:
Thank you so much Mikhail. 
I already have seen that specification, But those spec can't be understand easily. 
That's why I look your kind of `annotated`specification.

excerpts.content: you're welcome!
